STEP 1 - Scene: A small portion of a baked or stewed chicken-type dish with a tomato-based red sauce, served on a white square plate. Photographed from above, nearly top-down.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White square plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area of a 26 cm square-ish plate ≈ 26 x 26 x ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 575 cm^2. Use ~550 cm^2 as the working area.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Chicken pieces (skin-on, pieces of thigh/drumstick-like meat, visible at upper and left)
- Tomato-based sauce with some pepper bits (red/green pieces visible)
- Pale cooked item (possibly potato or onion/garlic pieces) mixed with the chicken
- Scattered sauce drips on the plate

STEP 4 - Area:
- Chicken pieces, upper cluster: ~9% of vessel (~50 cm^2)
- Chicken and sauce, lower cluster: ~10% (~55 cm^2)
- Scattered sauce drips: ~2% (~11 cm^2)
Total food coverage ≈ 21% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume (height ~1.5–2 cm for the piled areas, thin for drips):
- Upper cluster: 50 cm^2 x 1.5 cm = 75 ml
- Lower cluster: 55 cm^2 x 2 cm = 110 ml
- Drips: 11 cm^2 x 0.2 cm = 2 ml

STEP 6 - Grams (bulk density):
- Chicken and pale pieces, upper cluster (mixed, dense): 75 ml x 0.9 = 68 g
- Lower cluster, mixed meat and sauce: 110 ml x 0.9 = 99 g
- Sauce drips: 2 ml x 1.0 = 2 g

Split the combined 169 g of the two clusters into chicken and the pale starch/vegetable component:
- Chicken: ~110 g
- Pale pieces (potato/onion-like): ~30 g
- Tomato sauce with pepper: ~29 g (including drips)

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Chicken (cooked, skin-on): 110 g x 200 kcal/100g = 220 kcal
- Pale starchy pieces (potato-like, cooked): 30 g x 90 kcal/100g = 27 kcal
- Tomato sauce: 29 g x 60 kcal/100g = 17 kcal
Total ≈ 264 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 170 g of food across a fraction of the plate, with the plate mostly empty, is plausible for a partly eaten portion. Energy around 260 kcal is reasonable for this amount of chicken with sauce.
